notes: Resets every quarter (encodes quarter as a leading digit, e.g. 100101 = Q1 cluster01 hh01). NOT usable to link a household across quarters on its own. Kept only as a raw provenance field.

True within-cluster household serial number (stable across quarters in principle). Combine with cluster to form the household panel key. Despite the export column being named 'HholdID', it is the LAST TWO DIGITS of hhid, not a global household ID -- verified empirically (2022: matches hhid mod 100).
Enumeration area / cluster code. 600 unique values per year, matching the GSS catalogue figure. Used as the PSU for clustered SEs and as part of the household/person panel key.
Member line number within household (per quarter roster). 'new_pid' is a duplicate of this column (>99.7% identical across all 3 years) -- personid is used as canonical, new_pid dropped.
Duplicate of personid (kept out of the pipeline; documented so nobody re-derives it as a separate person key by mistake).
District code/name (value-labelled 'distcode'). Available for finer geography than region if needed.
16 regions incl. the 2018/2019 splits (Western North/Ahafo/Bono/Bono East/Oti/Savannah/North East). Value-labelled.
Urban/Rural (2 categories). Value-labelled.

No explicit design-stratum variable was found among the 838 exported columns (checked variable names and labels). GSS AHIES strata are conventionally region x locality (urbrur); use that as the clustered/stratified-SE proxy unless the GSS technical/DDI documentation names an explicit stratum id. Confirm before final SE computation.
2022 / 2023 / 2024. Set by which raw file the row came from -- never inferred from hhid, because hhid's leading digit is only a within-file quarter tag, not a year tag.
'2022Q1'...'2024Q4'. Kept as-is for a human-readable label.

1-4, the within-year time index t used by the estimator. NOT the same as the raw 'qtr' column, which is a running counter across all three files (1-4 in 2022, 5-8 in 2023, 9-12 in 2024) rather than a within-year index -- verified by crosstabbing year x qtr against the 'quarter' string column. t_within_year is instead parsed from the last character of 'quarter' (e.g. '2022Q1' -> 1), which is reliable regardless of year.
Person-level (population) sampling weight.
Household-level sampling weight.
Age in completed years.
Male / Female. Value-labelled; validated as time-invariant within-person (100% constant across quarters for linked individuals in 2022).
17-category relationship-to-head code. Value-labelled.
9-category marital status. Value-labelled.

'Never attended' / 'Attended in the past' / 'Attending now'. Missingness in s2aq3 lines up almost exactly with 'Never attended' (~20.7% of working-age rows in 2022), confirming s2aq3 is the general attainment item, not a current-enrolment-only item.
Highest level of schooling attending now / attended in the past. 16-category value label. Missing iff ever_attended_school == 'Never attended' (by construction/skip pattern, not a data-quality gap).
1-digit ISIC-style major division (21 categories, incl. Armed forces), main job only. Defined only when the person has a main job (see labour_status4).
1-digit ISCO-style major group (10 categories incl. Armed forces), main job only.
Count of roster rows sharing the same (year x quarter x cluster x HholdID).
Count of household members aged <15 in the same year x quarter x household.
Count of OTHER household members (excluding self) classified formally/informally employed in the same year x quarter x household.
GSS-derived ILO activity status: 'Employed' / 'Unemployed' / 'Not active'. 0% missing for working-age (15+) rows in every quarter checked (2022) -- this is the Gate 1 evidence.
GSS-derived 0/1 flag for having done any work in the reference period. Cross-check against econact.

ICSE-like status in main job (12 categories: paid employee, casual worker, paid/unpaid apprentice, agric/non-agric self-employed with/without employees, agric/non-agric contributing family worker, domestic worker, other). 0% missing among econact=='Employed' in 2022 -- this is the core Gate 3 item.

9-category institutional sector of the main job (Public/Semi-public/Private Formal/Private Informal/Local NGO/Intl NGO/Religious local/Religious intl/International org). 0% missing among the employed (main job) in 2022, including the self-employed -- this is what makes an enterprise-based informality route usable even where contract/SSNIT are skip-patterned to employees only.

'Yes, written' / 'Yes, verbal/oral' / 'No'. Universe = paid employee or casual worker (per s4aq46) ONLY -- ~99.3% non-missing within that universe in 2022, ~99.4% missing outside it. This is a GSS skip pattern, not a data-quality problem; do not treat non-employee missingness as informal by default without checking status_in_job first (the construction rule in scripts/construct.py handles this).
Yes/No, entitled to any social security benefit in main job. Same employee-only skip pattern as has_contract.

Yes/No SSNIT enrolment specifically. Populated only for the subset who answered Yes to social_security_entitled AND itemised SSNIT among benefit types -- ~92% missing even within paid employees in 2022. Too thin to use as the primary informality criterion on its own; used only as a supporting/robustness item, not the headline rule (see docs/codebook.md, Gate 3).

Cash payment amount for the main job, last pay period. Universe = paid employee/casual worker; ~80% missing among ALL employed in 2022 because only ~20% of the employed are wage employees -- expected, not a defect. Gate 5 verdict: usable only as a wage-subsample robustness variable, not a general covariate (matches the spec's own caution).
Pay period unit (daily/weekly/monthly/etc.) for payment_amount.
Total hours of work across all economic activities in the past 7 days -- the general actual-hours item (not job-specific).
Available for additional hours of work in the past 7 days -- feeds time-related underemployment.
